transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM); Michael Chen (Polaris Security Lead), Aisha Patel (IT Ops), Tom Reyes (Procurement), Nora Lim (Legal)

[00:00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time, um today we'll walk through the SIG/CAIQ and call out where you can find evidence in our portal and what the typical asks are for banks like you
[00:00:12] Michael (Polalis? transcription glitch): thanks, uh Polaris, um thanks Ethan, we wanna focus on data residency and keys primarily, and make sure procurement/legal have what they need
[00:00:20] Ethan: yep totally, we'll cover SOC 2/ISO reports up front, then SSO/SCIM, audit logs, encryption/KMS incl BYOK options, and then evidence locations. Sofia will run the technical bits.
[00:00:32] Sofia (Redwood SE): hi team, quick thing - forgive the background noise, um first big ticket: SOC 2 Type II, we have the report in the compliance portal and the certificate for ISO 27001, both are downloadable; we also keep a controls matrix that maps SIG questions to evidence artifacts
[00:00:45] Aisha (Polaris): can you confirm how recent the SOC 2 is? we need past 12 months and ideally the test period covering last quarter
[00:00:52] Sofia: yes it's 2025-11 audit period, Type II, covers controls through Oct 2025. we'll include the report and the complementary controls matrix.
[00:01:05] Tom (Procurement): procurement will need attestations for subcontractors and a list of subprocessors, is that in the SIG?
[00:01:12] Liam (Redwood CSM): yes, subprocessor list is maintained, we link to current vendors in the privacy and subprocessor doc. we'll attach that.

[00:02:00] Sofia: next SSO and RBAC — we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. we also have role-based access control configurable via the console and can emit SCIM membership changes to your IdP. some customers use SCIM downstream for provisioning into their entitlements platform
[00:02:18] Michael: how about session lifetime and MFA enforcement? we have strict MFA rules for admin roles
[00:02:23] Sofia: we recommend enforcing IdP-side MFA; for session timeouts we have configurable session settings on the control plane for admin sessions — default is 60 minutes but can be shortened. we store admin actions in audit logs.

[00:03:10] Nora (Legal): on SAML metadata exchange, is there support for certificate rotation without downtime?
[00:03:16] Sofia: yes, you can upload multiple certs and we support key rollover processes; we'll attach a short runbook.

[00:04:00] Ethan: switching to audit logs — what's the retention and format?
[00:04:05] Sofia: we keep audit logs for 365 days in our hosted offering; for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention — we typically recommend pulling to your SIEM (Splunk/QRadar/Datadog) via log streaming. logs include actor, action, resource, timestamp and request id; small note: some field names in the export use internal acronyms, so we'll include a mapping table
[00:04:30] Aisha: can we get real-time streaming for critical alerts?
[00:04:34] Sofia: yes, we have webhook/email/Syslog and a streaming endpoint for high-priority events; for Dedicated there's support for syslog over TLS into your collector.

[00:05:12] Tom: encryption specifics — at-rest, in-transit, and customer-managed keys?
[00:05:18] Sofia: all data is encrypted in transit via TLS 1.2+ and at rest using AES-256. for hosted customers we manage keys in our cloud KMS; for Dedicated or Private customers we support BYOK where you bring keys via KMS/HSM integration (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). key rotation policies are configurable and we log key usage events in the audit trail
[00:05:45] Michael: if we request BYOK, does Redwood have access to plaintext ever?
[00:05:50] Sofia: no, with BYOK the encryption keys are under your control; our runtime uses the key for decryption in memory as needed but we don't retain customer keys; we can provide a whitepaper on our memory and key handling. we'll include the HSM/KMS architecture diagram.

[00:07:00] Ethan: data residency — Polaris needs EU and US-only residency for certain regulated datasets, is that feasible?
[00:07:08] Sofia: yes we can pin data to regions; options: hosted with region controls, Dedicated with region-specific pools, or Private deployment in your VPC/on-prem. for strict residency we'll recommend Dedicated or Private and we can show network diagrams and routing policies
[00:07:26] Michael: do you provide customer-managed audit logs stored in our region?
[00:07:30] Sofia: for Dedicated/Private yes — logs can be stored in-region or exported to your SIEM in-region; for hosted we store logs per region but exports may traverse endpoints based on integration config — we'll clarify in the evidence pack.

[00:08:10] Tom: vendor questionnaire specifics — in the SIG some questions ask for screenshots of config pages and runbooks, is that ok?
[00:08:17] Ethan: that's fine, we provide redacted screenshots and runbook excerpts; where needed we provide sanitized logs for evidence, and artifacts are delivered via secure share (ShareFile or similar) with expiring links

[00:09:00] Aisha: request — can you show our security team the network diagram and the VPC peering flow?
[00:09:05] Sofia: yes I'll attach a diagram, it includes subnet flows, NAT/egress, and private endpoints. note: some internal hostnames are redacted in shared diagrams

[00:10:00] Ethan: quick note re: SOC 2 mapping — the SIG has many control-level asks, we map them to our control IDs in the controls matrix; you'll see the evidence column with a link to the artifact and a short description
[00:10:15] Michael: about patching and vulnerability management — can you confirm cadence and whether you run external scans?
[00:10:21] Sofia: we have weekly patch windows for infra and monthly for non-critical app updates; we run quarterly external vuln scans and annual pen tests; for Dedicated/Private customers we can coordinate maintenance windows to fit your SLAs

[00:11:30] Nora: legal wants to confirm incident response SLA and breach notification timelines
[00:11:36] Liam: our standard incident response is to notify customers within 72 hours for confirmed data incidents, with a dedicated incident runbook and postmortem. for enterprise contracts we can negotiate tighter timelines and dedicated incident contacts.

[00:12:40] Michael: regulators sometimes ask for encryption key custody details — can you provide an attestation for BYOK handling?
[00:12:46] Ethan: yes we'll include a BYOK attestation document and the KMS/HSM integration whitepaper; Sofia will include the key usage log schema.

[00:13:50] Sofia: on RBAC, we support customizable roles and granular permissions; you can create admin, developer, auditor roles. account-level audit logs include role changes, and we offer an RBAC export for third-party governance tools
[00:14:10] Aisha: is schema for logs compatible with our SIEM? field names, timestamps etc?
[00:14:15] Sofia: yes exports are JSON/NDJSON and map to common SIEM fields; we'll include an example export and field mapping in the packet

[00:15:30] Tom: procurement will want proof of insurance and subcontractor agreements
[00:15:35] Liam: we'll attach current insurance certificates and the subprocessor list; note that some subprocessor agreements are redacted for NDA reasons but we provide summary attestations

[00:16:40] Ethan: let's go through a couple of tricky SIG items live — question 4.2 around key rotation, what do you want to assert?
[00:16:47] Michael: we need specifics: rotation frequency, emergency rotation playbook, and validation steps
[00:16:52] Sofia: rotation frequency for customer-managed KMS is controlled by you; for our managed keys we rotate yearly and maintain a documented rotation playbook; emergency rotation is a documented runbook that includes revocation, re-issuance, and re-encryption steps — we'll attach excerpts and the verification checklist

[00:18:20] Ethan: question 7.1 about log tamper detection — do you produce WORM or signed log options?
[00:18:25] Sofia: we offer append-only storage with signed checksums for critical audit events; additional tamper detection can be achieved by streaming to your SIEM with immutable storage there; we'll indicate that in our SIG answer

[00:20:00] Aisha: what about background checks for employees with access to logs or keys?
[00:20:06] Liam: employees in sensitive roles go through background checks per our HR policy; we'll include the relevant HR controls summary

[00:22:15] Nora: on data deletion and retention, if we request deletion for certain datasets, how is that handled across caches or backups?
[00:22:22] Sofia: deletion is handled at the object level; for KV caches there's an eviction policy and for backups we have retention windows — for hard deletes we provide a documented process and timeline; some remnants may persist in immutable backups until retention expiry, we document that in the deletion policy

[00:24:00] Ethan: flurry of quick clarifications — do you need a signed NDA to get some of the redacted artifacts?
[00:24:05] Michael: yes for some artifacts we do require a mutual NDA
[00:24:10] Ethan: okay we can route the NDA to Nora and Tom; once executed we'll share sensitive diagrams and sanitized logs

[00:25:00] Sofia: one technical note — for Private deployments we support full air-gap options but that increases onboarding time and requires our deployment team onsite or in your environment; we usually do a 6-12 week plan depending on scope
[00:25:18] Michael: that's fine, we expected that timeline

[00:26:00] Tom: pricing question for Dedicated with BYOK and extended log retention? rough delta?
[00:26:06] Ethan: cost depends on committed capacity and retention window; BYOK itself is not a large cost but Dedicated capacity and extended retention for logs increases monthly commitments — we'll include an indicative pricing addendum with the SIG packet

[00:27:30] Aisha: any compliance automation around evidence collection?
[00:27:34] Sofia: yes our controls matrix is exportable and we can pre-populate SIG answers with links to artifacts; for large customers we provide a shared evidence bucket and short-lived links for retrieval

[00:29:00] Ethan: let's summarize next steps
[00:29:04] Ethan: Redwood to: 1) upload completed SIG/CAIQ answers with links to SOC 2, ISO cert, subprocessor list and redacted screenshots; 2) Sofia to attach technical diagrams (VPC/peering, KMS flow, key rotation runbook); 3) Polaris to confirm residency + list of regulated datasets; 4) route NDA to Nora for redacted artifacts. schedule follow-up week of 2026-02-29 to go through submitted evidence
[00:29:35] Michael: sounds good, thanks everyone
[00:29:40] Nora: will review NDA and loop legal in
[00:29:45] Tom: procurement will review pricing addendum once shared

[00:30:00] Ethan: any remaining Qs?
[00:30:05] Michael: one small one — can you provide an example of the audit export size and retention storage overhead?
[00:30:12] Sofia: example exports avg ~500MB/day for medium-volume accounts; varies a lot by event verbosity; we'll include sample metrics and cost estimates for retention in the packet

[00:31:00] Ethan: great, we'll send the packet and follow up. thanks all

[00:31:10] Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional misattributed speaker names (Polalis -> Polaris) and small filler words left in. Artifacts referenced: SOC2-TypeII.pdf, ISO27001-certificate.pdf, controls-matrix.xlsx, subprocessor-list.pdf, vpc-diagram.pdf, kms-key-rotation.pdf, nda-template.pdf
